items.t: High-voltage battery fire risk
items.job: Replace high-voltage battery pack or modules
items.note: Free under GM's battery recall. Check your VIN. Many 2020-2022 cars only needed diagnostic software, not a new battery.

items.t: Battery monitoring software not installed correctly
items.job: Reprogram battery and hybrid control modules (BECM, HPCM2, BCM)
items.note: Free software recall. Check your VIN or ask a Chevrolet EV dealer.

items.t: Sudden loss of power with charge still showing
items.job: Diagnose and update battery control software
items.note: Ask the dealer; bulletins and the battery warranty often cover it. Replacing a weak battery module costs much more.

items.t: Seat belt pretensioner can ignite carpet after a crash
items.job: Install heat-shield foil and pretensioner covers near B-pillars
items.note: Free under GM's recall, even if done once before. Check your VIN.

items.t: Rear brake calipers may lose braking force
items.job: Bleed brake system
items.note: The recall remedy is a free brake bleed. Check your VIN. Replacing rear calipers costs more.

items.t: Rear door may open unexpectedly
items.job: Replace rear inside door handle cables
items.note: Free under GM's recall. Check your VIN or ask a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: Front left brake caliper may crack
items.job: Free recall repair at a Chevrolet dealer: inspect and replace front left brake caliper if affected
items.note: Free under GM safety recall (NHTSA 20V-808). Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: Seat belt may not be properly anchored
items.job: Free recall repair at a Chevrolet dealer: inspect seat belt anchor bolts and replace with correct bolts
items.note: Free under GM safety recall (NHTSA 20V-811). Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: Driver airbag may not be secured
items.job: Free recall repair at a Chevrolet dealer: inspect and secure driver airbag fasteners
items.note: Free under GM safety recall (NHTSA 21V-517). Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy correctly
items.job: Free recall repair at a Chevrolet dealer: inspect and repair or replace instrument panel
items.note: Free under GM safety recall (NHTSA 23V-567). Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: 12-volt battery dies and car will not turn on
items.job: Replace 12-volt AGM auxiliary battery
items.note: Same figures as this model's maintenance cost for the 12-volt battery. A jump start and battery test may be all that is needed if the battery is still good.

items.t: A/C stops blowing cold
items.job: Find A/C leak, replace leaking refrigerant line, evacuate and recharge
items.note: Based on RepairPal (2021 Bolt EV): refrigerant line $540-$749 plus evacuate and recharge $332-$412; the parts and hours split is approximate. Replacing the electric A/C compressor costs more and may be covered by the EV component warranty.

items.t: Car will not charge from a home or public charger
items.job: Diagnose charging fault (onboard charger, cord or outlet)
items.note: Diagnosis only, because the fix depends on whether the cord, outlet or car is at fault. RepairPal electrical diagnosis: $122-$179. If the onboard charger is replaced, the GM part is about $605-$970 before labor and is usually covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile EV component warranty.

items.t: Loss of drive power from a failed battery disconnect relay
items.job: Diagnose high-voltage loss of propulsion
items.note: Diagnosis only, because the fix depends on which high-voltage part failed. RepairPal electrical diagnosis: $122-$179. The battery disconnect junction block is about $483-$763 from GM; this repair is normally covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile EV component warranty. Towing is extra.

items.t: Clicking or clunking from front stabilizer links
items.job: Replace front stabilizer bar link
items.note: Based on YourMechanic: $188-$208 per link installed (shop/dealer $222-$319). Owners report aftermarket links at about $10-$11 each. Price is per side.

items.t: Touchscreen freezes or loses settings
items.job: Diagnose and reprogram radio/display software
items.note: Diagnosis and software only, because some cars need a display module instead. RepairPal electrical diagnosis: $122-$179. Software updates may be free under warranty.

items.t: Rusted brake rotors from light brake use
items.job: Replace front brake pads and rotors
items.note: Same figures as this model's front brake maintenance cost. Rear pads and rotors cost about the same again. One owner paid $167 for all four rotors and pads (parts, likely DIY).

items.t: Portable charge cord shows a fault or will not charge
items.job: Replace portable dual-level charge cord set
items.note: Owner-reported prices: about $344 for a new dual-level cord plus $108 for the 120V adapter, or about $442 at a dealer. Covered under the bumper-to-bumper warranty when it is a defect.

items.t: Portable charge cord may not cut power if ground is lost (recall)
items.job: Free recall: inspect portable charge cord serial number and replace if affected
items.note: Free under GM recall N232407300 (NHTSA 23E-065). Check your VIN or bring the cord to a Chevrolet dealer.

items.t: Hum or drone from the front at highway speed
items.job: Remove front fascia and add foam tape to the air baffle (bulletin 22-NA-024)
items.note: Labor time from GM bulletin 22-NA-024. Covered under bumper-to-bumper warranty if the car is still within it.
